subject: FinLytics — follow-up on token economics & benchmarking
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Claire Johnson <claire@finlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: FinLytics — follow-up on token economics & benchmarking

Hi Claire — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we have aligned expectations on pricing and volume for the POC: 

Recap of what you shared:
- Product: FinLytics contextual assistant embedded in your web product (help & insights panes).
- Traffic profile: target pilot ~50k DAU across US / EU, variable peak days.
- Typical session: ~300–500 tokens in generation+context per session.
- Current rough estimate: 200M–800M tokens/month in pilot (you mentioned a wide initial range).
- Important: budget sensitivity — finance expects cost per 1M tokens to be competitive with OpenAI/Anthropic benchmarks.

As discussed, could you confirm the following so we can surface a concrete pricing band: 
1) A narrower monthly token estimate if possible (low / expected / high).
2) Target budget range or target $/1M tokens you’re hoping to hit for the pilot.
3) Any hard constraints (SLA, data residency, encryption) that would change pricing (e.g., require Private deployment).

What I’ll do next:
- Share a short mutual action plan (MAP) and a market-compare brief showing $/1M token benchmarks vs OpenAI/Anthropic and two self-hosting references.
- Loop Sergio (SE) to recommend model/quantization and cost levers (batching, prefix caching).
- Propose a pricing band for hosted POC and a preliminary committed rate for Dedicated if you prefer predictable unit economics.

If you can drop the narrower token numbers and any target $/1M today, I’ll draft the MAP and a provisional price table by end of day.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: FinLytics-usage-profiles.csv (CSV - referenced)

From: Claire Johnson <claire@finlytics.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@finlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinLytics — follow-up on token economics & benchmarking

Hi Rafael — great recap, thanks. I confirmed numbers with product/finance and here is a tighter projection for pilot (30–60 day scope):

Usage profile (pilot):
- Low: 120M tokens/month (20k DAU, conservative engagement)
- Expected: 420M tokens/month (50k DAU, median sessions ~350 tokens)
- High: 1.1B tokens/month (peak with marketing push)

Budget guardrail: finance has signaled we should target <= $12 / 1M tokens for the pilot to stay within internal ROI thresholds. They understand open-model hosts vary; our goal is to see something competitive versus managed vendors.

Benchmark notes we pulled:
- OpenAI (public pricing we referenced): ~ $18-$25 / 1M tokens depending on model & rates.
- Anthropic: ~ $14-$20 / 1M for comparable models in our tests.
- Self-hosted (incl. infra + ops estimates): ~ $6-$10 / 1M but requires engineering overhead and larger committed capacity.

We’re open to a hosted POC if the unit economics land near $10-$12 / 1M with predictable burst handling. If you can propose a two-tier band (hosted POC rate vs. committed Dedicated rate) that would be helpful.

Also attaching the usage CSV I mentioned.

Claire Johnson
Head of Product, FinLytics
Attachments: FinLytics-usage-profiles.csv (CSV)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Claire Johnson <claire@finlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 12:18:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: FinLytics — follow-up on token economics & benchmarking

Forwarding Claire’s tighter projection (see below). Finance is eyeballing <= $12/1M for pilot; customer prefers hosted POC if we can get near $10-$12/1M. 

Two asks for SE/Commercial:
- Sergio: can you draft a hosted POC cost estimate (per 1M token bands) with recommended model variant, caching strategy, and realistic latency SLOs for 400-token average sessions? Please include where caching/batching can reduce effective tokens.
- Monica: propose a short price band we can present (hosted POC vs Dedicated commit). If Dedicated, what commit level would get us into ~$6-$8/1M territory?

I’ll prepare a MAP after we land on numbers. Attaching the MAP template and the usage file Claire provided.

— Rafael

Attachments: FinLytics-MAP-v0.3.pdf (PDF)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: FinLytics — follow-up on token economics & benchmarking

Rafael / Monica — quick SE notes and a rough pricing sketch for the pilot.

Technical assumptions (pilot POC):
- Model: Redwood-curated 13B quantized variant (low-latency), or Anthropic-equivalent if customer prefers.
- Avg session tokens: 350 generation + 50 context(average KV cache hit reduces repeat context).
- Effective tokens after caching: ~15–25% reduction for repeat queries across sessions with same user context.
- Target p95 latency: 350–500ms for 400-token generations on hosted endpoints with continuous batching.

Pricing sketch (hosted POC - ballpark) per 1M tokens:
- Baseline hosted (on-demand): $12 / 1M tokens (recommended starting band)
- Optimized hosted (with prefix caching & batching + careful model choice): $9 / 1M tokens
- Dedicated (reserved capacity, 12mo commit): $6 / 1M tokens (requires 250M+ committed monthly average to reach)

Notes on how we get there: quantized model variants + prefix/KV caching reduces total generation tokens; batching improves GPU utilization to lower unit cost. Dedicated pricing assumes a multi-month commit and cross-region flexibility.

I’ll attach a quick CSV with cost curves by monthly volume and commit level. Recommend we open with the $9–12 band for hosted POC and show a path to $6/1M with Dedicated at scale.

— Sergio
SE, Redwood Inference
Attachments: pricing_estimate_FINLYTICS.csv (CSV)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Claire Johnson <claire@finlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 17:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinLytics — follow-up on token economics & benchmarking

Claire — thanks for the quick confirmation and the CSV. Based on the numbers above and SE input, here are proposed next steps and a provisional price band for the pilot: 

Provisional pricing (to present to finance):
- Hosted POC (no commit): $9–12 / 1M tokens.
  - Target: $12 baseline, $9 if we optimize model/caching during the POC.
- Dedicated (12mo commit, 250M+ avg/month): ~$6 / 1M tokens (we’d build a committed pricing table with ramp down tiers).

Why this is competitive:
- OpenAI/Anthropic: public managed prices are generally higher for comparable managed endpoints (~$14–25/1M depending on model/throughput).
- Self-hosted: lower infra-only cost in some scenarios (~$6–10/1M) but carries engineering/ops risk and slower time-to-market.

Suggested next steps:
1) Schedule a 30-min pricing + MAP review tomorrow to align finance and scope — I’ll propose two time windows.
2) We’ll deliver a one-page market-compare brief and a draft MAP showing milestones, success metrics, and acceptance criteria (attached: redwood-vs-market-brief.pdf, MAP template).
3) If you want, we can start the hosted POC immediately with a 2-week pilot and the $12 baseline while we optimize for $9.

Would you prefer we present the hosted POC band to finance as $9–12 or lead with $12 baseline then show the optimized path to $9?

Thanks again — Rafael
Attachments: redwood-vs-market-brief.pdf (PDF), FinLytics-MAP-v0.3.pdf (PDF)
